title: How to Use Automation for High and Low Season
summary: See how to adapt automation rules for high and low season shifts in a short-stay operation.
body_markdown:
Using automation for high and low season means the same underlying process adapts its rules — pricing triggers, staffing alerts, communication frequency — based on the season, instead of manually reconfiguring the operation twice a year. In **Jestor** , conditional automation handles this kind of seasonal variation.


Short-stay operations genuinely behave differently in high versus low season, which means treating both periods identically wastes effort in one and under-resources the other.


## What seasonal shifts complicate without adaptive automation


- The same staffing and communication rules applied regardless of actual demand
- Manual reconfiguration of processes twice a year, prone to being forgotten
- No automatic distinction between high-season urgency and low-season routine
- Pricing or availability rules that don't adjust automatically with the season


## How seasonal conditional automation works


- Conditions can check the current date range and adjust automation behavior accordingly
- Staffing alerts or task priority can shift automatically between seasons
- Communication frequency or template content can vary by season
- Pricing-related triggers can reflect high- and low-season rules without manual toggling


## Why Jestor fits this use case


- Conditional logic handles seasonal variation within the same overall process
- No manual reconfiguration required twice a year — rules adjust automatically
- The same underlying structure supports both high- and low-season operation
- Reduces the risk of forgetting to switch modes at the season transition


Season Automation behavior


High season Higher urgency thresholds, faster staffing alerts


Low season Adjusted communication frequency, routine priority


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Does this require manually switching modes at season transitions?** No, conditional rules based on dates can handle the transition automatically. More at[jestor.com](https://www.jestor.com/?ref=blog.jestor.com) .


**Can pricing rules differ by season?** Yes, through conditional logic tied to date ranges.


**Does this require rebuilding the process for each season?** No, it's the same process with conditional variation built in.
